title: Use the festival
steps: Notice the archetype behind a holiday such as Christmas
Ask what it says about your own soul
Use the softer, more open mood of the days for inner work
why: Every great festival encodes an archetype of the soul's journey, and people open up during festive days.

title: Read pain as an alarm clock
steps: When pain, loss or grief arrives, pause
Ask what condition it is calling you to change
why: Pain in becoming is the soul's wake-up call out of sleep.

title: Die a little every day
steps: Each day pick one identification: a role, label, belief or bodily image
Release it
Ask: what am I beyond what I seem to be?
why: Philosophy is practice of dying, and Socrates says both 'dying' and 'being dead' because it is daily.

title: Start from not knowing
steps: Begin with 'I know that I do not know'
Empty out what school, news, TV and socialisation taught as truth
why: Truth, like death, is subtractive.

title: Μύω: close the senses
steps: Close the eyes and the mouth
Turn away from the senses
Go inward
why: Initiation (μύησις) begins with μύω, and from it comes the pregnancy (κύησις) of the soul.

title: Protect what is gestating
steps: Stay quiet, humble and close
Take only pure 'food' on every level
Avoid quarrels and shadow-boxing with those still bound
Do not be discouraged if called mad
why: The embryo of awakening is vulnerable and must be hidden from what mocks or threatens it.

title: In the labour
steps: Surrender
Do not fear
Push
Have a good midwife: a teacher or helper
why: Then the birth into light can happen at its ripe hour.

title: Rest after awakening
steps: After an opening, stay a while
Let yourself be nourished and strengthened before acting
why: Like a newborn's 40 days, the new consciousness needs ῥῶσις, strengthening.

title: Say 'my dear One'
steps: At the tax office, on the road when cut off, in heated debates
Silently greet the One there
Remind yourself: 'one more game'
why: Immanence means recognising the One in everything, including what annoys us.

title: Act from the inner sun
steps: Take positions and help others awaken
Check that the action springs from remembered unity
Avoid both nihilism and hedonism
why: Action rooted in pure being unites rather than divides.

title: Ask about your relationship with yourself
steps: Ask how you relate to yourself
Ask how far you have turned your soul's eye inward
Make an 'inner dive' and ask who you are
why: Εὖ ζῆν depends on this relationship, not on achievements.

title: Choose helpers well
steps: Look for a therapist, teacher or guide whose motive is pure
Prefer someone who has walked the path
Still do the inner work yourself
why: No one can lead you on a path they have not crossed, and no one can walk it for you.

title: Turn βίος into ζωή
steps: Ask what you love to do
Ask what inspires you
Ask how you can benefit society
Follow your 'deep heartbeat'
why: Life becomes conscious when it follows νόησις, λόγος and love rather than instinct and routine.

title: Find your mast
steps: Notice how a honk or a setback throws you up and down
Cultivate a central inner axis instead
why: Eudaimonia is staying at your mast while fortune's wheel turns.

title: Open the treasure chest
steps: Study the Greek philosophical tradition
Practise it as a way of life, not as information
why: Greeks sit on a treasure chest of spiritual wealth they rarely open.

title: Treat shocks as ἐξαίφνης
steps: When a crisis or a great love arrives, ask what it is waking
Remember every situation has an exit of freedom
why: The sudden event is how cosmic law shakes a boxed life awake.

title: Depression as deep rest
steps: See it as the soul's cry to be freed
Allow 'deep rest'
Seek help so you do not get lost there
why: Depression can be a spiritual surgery for a mask that has stuck.

title: Celebrate life
steps: Refuse the lie that life is to be endured
Honour it, use it creatively, celebrate it
why: Εὖ ζῆν is a feast.

title: Go along with things
steps: Practise awareness and presence
Notice where each impulse comes from: truth, falsehood, sleep, desire, emotion, programme
why: Σύνεσις is going with the flow of things, alert like a good general.

title: Gestate knowledge
steps: Take one seed or idea
Carry it and give it time
Let love drive the learning
why: Information is not knowledge; knowledge must be born in you.

title: Leave the door open
steps: Start by truly wanting change
Leave a little room for eros
why: Even the universe respects free will; wanting turns the wheels of soul and life.

title: From pride to gratitude
steps: Be grateful for what parents, grandparents and the past gave
Then go deeper: study and live it
why: Fireworks give birth to nothing new; a good root must sprout.

title: Sit with your conscience
steps: Spend time alone without phone or TV
Let repressed material surface
Listen to the voice of conscience
why: Solitude brings movement toward the new, though at first you must 'enter the war'.

title: Respect shame
steps: Say: I'm human, I erred, I deceived myself here
Ask what you can learn
Adjust and move on
why: Αἰσχύνην σέβου replaces self-flagellation with a healthy dialogue with conscience.

title: Who plays the roles?
steps: Ask who you are beyond all your roles and garments
Notice how many things pull at your attention in a day
See how you build a role for each and lock into it
why: Recognising the actor behind the roles is the vision of the spectacle.

title: Watch your thoughts
steps: Observe your thoughts and when you think them
Notice which beliefs you hold
Ask whether each is necessary
why: Each stage of the cave is a mode of mind to deconstruct.

title: Train with a sensible example
steps: Take something visible: sunlight, the eye, a solstice
Use it as a παράδειγμα to grasp the invisible
why: Plato's ἀναγωγή climbs from the sensible to the intelligible.

title: Fall in love with the Good
steps: Let yourself be 'sufficiently disappointed by becoming'
Rank the Good first, above everything
why: Eros cannot be engineered, but you can let the flame catch.

title: Practise ἀπάθεια
steps: Do not invest your happiness in whether things go well
Do not invest it in what others do or don't do
why: Marcus Aurelius' non-reactivity is steadiness, not indifference.

title: Return after the opening
steps: Go back to work, loved ones and admin
Practise seeing the One and the fire there
why: Initiation is complete only with immanence.

title: Drop the need to be right
steps: Catch yourself wanting to be proved right
Remember you have probably lost justice
Aim for balance instead
why: Justice is collective balance held from the middle.

title: Do not wrong yourself
steps: Start with how you treat yourself
Before acting, ask which act serves collective harmony and εὖ ζῆν
why: Injustice to oneself radiates outward as an energy.

title: Set your intention
steps: Before any inquiry, state your intention
Notice how it shapes your position and your vision
why: Πρόθεσις determines θέσις, which determines θέασις.

title: Take one key home
steps: From any teaching, choose one key
Apply it in daily life
why: Philosophy is a way of living each moment, not discussion.

title: Attune at the solstices
steps: Treat solstices and equinoxes as days of heightened energy
Use them for attunement
why: The ancient festival calendar was built around them.

title: Speak the language of unity
steps: Hold that something is always the same and never the same
Avoid the reflex of 'A or B'
why: Unity does not split into opposites.

title: Touch rather than grasp
steps: Seek to touch and be kindled by the truth
Do not try to pin it down with thought
why: Ἅπτω means both to touch and to kindle.

title: Look for what wears the soul
steps: Go beyond studying desire, emotion and thought
Look for the fiery awareness at their core
why: That is the meaning of γνῶθι σαυτόν.

title: Dry the passions
steps: Notice fear, anger, jealousy and envy as wet, sticky states
Turn inward and contact the forms
Cultivate virtue and justice
why: The dry soul is wisest and best.

title: Melt the ice cube
steps: Drop the image of yourself as a separate frozen form
Remember yourself as one field in many forms
why: Separate forms are at war; remembering unity is freedom.

title: Take political responsibility
steps: Notice when you say 'I'm not political'
Remember politics includes how you judge and think
Act at your own scale: town, village, community
Help create spaces where people exercise logos together
why: Abstaining is itself a political stance and a surrender of our nature.

title: Look behind inherited words
steps: Take words like democracy, citizen, paideia
Ask what practices and states of consciousness they first meant
why: Same words can hide a changed consciousness.

title: The apophatic test
steps: When you think 'this is it', pause
Ask whether you are still seeing or understanding 'something'
If so, do not stop: you have not reached Ithaca
why: The One is no 'something', so any object, even God or light, is not yet it.

title: Enjoy experiences without mistaking them
steps: Welcome visions, energy or an opening heart in meditation
Treat them as steps
Do not confuse them with awakening
why: They are useful stages, but every experience is within the finite.

title: Stop the 'if... then' bargain
steps: Notice thoughts like 'after one more book, concept, trip or initiation, then...'
Recognise them as postponement into an imagined future
Turn to now
why: The only right moment is now; even spiritual methods can become the last obstacle.

title: Drop the checklist of the awakened
steps: Stop judging yourself or others by aura, diet, speech or lifestyle
Do not call yourself awakened
why: Awakening has no objective traits, and the belief 'I am awakened' shows the separate someone still stands.

title: Play your roles without identifying
steps: Keep your duties, even strict or serious ones
Play them consciously
Keep the inner lightness of the eternal child
why: You play the role; you are not the role.

title: Re-centre your goals
steps: Keep aims and pursuits
Take yourself out of the centre
Put the whole, Hestia, the One there
Work for the benefit, freedom and awakening of all beings
why: Ego-goals serve someone who does not exist; the awakened become κόσμιος and πολιτικός.

title: Purify the senses with each contact
steps: With each sensation, remember consciousness is behind it
Ask: what am I receiving, what satisfies me, what do I lose?
Approach what benefits (ὠφέλιμον), avoid what harms (βλαβερόν)
why: The senses are a path of purification, not something to escape.

title: Seek the calm
steps: Choose quiet surroundings when you can
Let the soul's motions 'take advantage of the calm'
why: Calm lets the soul's circles recover their order and judgment become correct, as the Pythagoreans knew.

title: Remember your essence when shaken
steps: When a sight or scent shakes or elates you, notice it
Recall that only the soul's revolutions are moved, not its essence
why: Equanimity is revealed, not built.

title: Treat desire as longing for the divine
steps: Notice a desire
Ask what fullness it is really seeking
Look for that fullness within
Use the senses as allies, not as the route
why: Behind every desire the soul seeks the Good.

title: Use pure scents
steps: Prefer flowers, incense and herbs
Be wary of synthetic perfumes and animal-derived ingredients
Ask what your scents and exhalations 'feed'
why: Pure scent lifts the soul and cleanses the aura; mixed scent drags it down.

title: Use sparks and mirrors
steps: Use aromas, images and the arts as ἐναύσματα (sparks)
Let them remind you of the inner source
Remove the pebbles around the spring and let it gush
why: What we seek outside is already within.

title: One minute of gratitude
steps: Before study, pause for a minute
Recognise your ripened desire for freedom
Recognise your access to a teaching and your companions
why: Gratitude is the key that opens the path of liberation and eudaimonia.

title: Write your intention
steps: Ask: why am I here, what do I truly want from this journey?
Write it in a notebook
Revisit it at the end
why: To see whether your motive has been transformed, fulfilled or has vanished.

title: Listen as if for the first time
steps: Drop the sense that you already know this
Hear it fresh
why: You never step into the same river twice; no one has heard this lesson before.

title: Ask 'ποία χρεία;'
steps: Of any knowledge, ask what use it has
Ask what it changes in lived experience
why: Socrates disliked idle philosophising; knowledge must serve life.

title: Eyes open, eyes closed
steps: Open your eyes and note 'something, something, many somethings'
Close them and ask: is there 'something', or a boundless expanse?
Expect darkness at first; with training it becomes luminous
why: Paideia trains the inner seeing that everyone has and few use.

title: Practise aporia
steps: Start from 'I do not know'
Set aside prior knowledge
Do not turn truth into a banner
why: Renouncing knowledge is the beginning of knowledge.

title: Greek mindfulness
steps: Notice moment by moment how your consciousness is working
Name it: 'now I function this way, now that way'
Bring it from unconscious to conscious
why: This is walking toward the cave's exit.

title: Where is the cave?
steps: Reflect on where the cave is: outside you or inside
If inside, ask what the shadows, fire, objects and puppeteers are in you
Stop blaming outer puppeteers
why: If the puppeteer is within, there is no one outside to accuse.

title: Follow the why
steps: Take any choice: car, partner, job
Ask why, and again why
Continue until you reach the root wish
why: Every act aims finally at eudaimonia.

title: Live by the turnings
steps: Align your life and festivals with nature's rhythms and the four turnings
Use equinoxes to sow intentions
Use solstices as fertile gates
Remember the best moment is always now
why: Re-attuning to natural rhythm pulls you out of the cave; like the gym, no one can do it for you.

title: Descend with the hero's torch
steps: Turn inward in the dark season
Find your monsters and passions
Trace their roots in events, family and ancestors
Look at them face to face, without fear, wishing for transformation
Uproot them and sow virtues
why: Simply facing what you find begins the alchemy of catharsis.

title: Light or nothing
steps: At rock bottom, do not quit
Stay at the height of your soul, Mnemosyne
why: You are reborn in a way no one could have staged; trauma becomes θαῦμα.

title: Hierarchise your eros
steps: Name your desires
Place love of your Self, freedom and eudaimonia above them all
why: Only the one in love enough endures every trial.

title: Listen with the heart
steps: Hear a definition, such as Plato's on time
Pause in silence before interpreting
why: Some truths open only when received in silence.

title: Do not complain about the middle
steps: Welcome moderate circumstances
why: The mean helps the soul's two circles meet in an inner equinox.

title: Study and practise together
steps: Pair scholarship with daily meditation
Explore the nature of your energy, mind and self
Read poetry alongside philosophy
why: Analysis alone will not do it; poetry comes closest to the ineffable.

title: Practise equal care
steps: Notice whose well-being you count
Treat others' well-being as equal to your own
why: If we are one being, selective openness makes no sense.

title: Keep on going
steps: When the path is hard, do not stop
why: Her advice to her younger self: you will find the way.

title: Ether meditation on the space of awareness
steps: With eyes open, observe the objects in the room and their relation to you
Shift attention from the objects to the space they sit in; notice body relax, heart open, gaze widen
Close the eyes, connect with the breath, feel the inner space
Place one short thought or image at the centre of the mind-screen and breathe with it
Shift attention from that object to the space in which it appears, which remains before and after thoughts
Recognise its qualities: vastness, openness, soft aliveness, luminosity, eternity; recognise it as the I that sees and hears
Feel that space through neck, heart, hands, torso, belly, back, legs and soles: the space breathes the body
Let body, consciousness, space and I merge into the present; inner and outer space are one
Open the eyes and keep the recognition as forms resume their play
why: Ether, the fifth element and Plato's element of the gods, is treated as space and consciousness; the practice moves from objects to the awareness that holds them.

title: Chanting ὄν
steps: Chant on
Feel the N vibrate on the palate
Rest in the vibration
why: The N is primordial vibration, the One becoming being.

title: Guard what you listen to
steps: Notice the music and sounds you take in daily
Choose what you listen to with care
why: Listening is the most important spiritual act: sound flows straight into the soul and shapes ethos.

title: Visit ancient sites as living temples
steps: Approach the site with reverence
Open heart, mind and body
Sense the etheric temple beyond the ruins
why: The physical temples are ruins, but their etheric temples are untouched.

title: Marry reading with practice
steps: Read the non-dual texts analytically
Pair the reading with embodied practice and meditation
Read again from the shining of awareness, not the dual mind alone
why: These texts cannot be understood by the dual mind alone.

title: Read the Republic three times
steps: Read Plato's Republic cover to cover
Repeat at least three times
Only then debate it
why: It is an ark of knowledge that rewards full immersion.

title: Keep asking the adolescent questions
steps: Ask who am I
Ask why am I here
Ask what existence is for
Keep asking throughout life
why: These questions start the path that leads to self-knowledge.

title: Become a naked soul
steps: Notice the roles and suits you wear
Take them off one by one
Meet your fiery essence beneath them
why: Union requires shedding everything we are not (after Proclus).

title: Know your three selves
steps: Tell the story of your small self: birthplace, degrees, relationships
Study your soul's faculties: mind, heart, will, appetite
Seek the secret self, yourself as the One
why: Self-knowledge moves inward like a walk into a temple.

title: Hellenic mindfulness
steps: Before acting, study your motivation and energy
During the act, keep watching them
After the act, review them
why: A Pythagorean practice that purifies the passions and steers action to the good.

title: Purify before theory
steps: Train critical thinking to clear biases and dogmas
Purify greed, jealousy and anger; loosen materialism
Use diet, mantras and energy work
Approach mathematics and dialectics only with right motivation
why: The virtue ladder puts purification before theory, and knowledge without virtue is dangerous.

title: The eros of the question
steps: Turn attention from outside to inside
Ask who am I
Ask what is this consciousness through which I experience the universe
Notice it is not enclosed in your name
why: Each question opens an inner space leading from personality to soul to common consciousness.

title: Love in four registers
steps: Give a good word to all
Think well of all (ἀγαθοὶ λογισμοί)
Feel love toward all
Help all in action
Treat everything as your own household, selflessly
why: This is the natural ethics of one who sees consciousness as common.

title: Open love in stages
steps: Love a partner and family
Love the values, institutions and laws of your city
Love the universe
why: Eros grows from private to political to cosmic.

title: Answer harm with teaching
steps: Do not become indignant with people
Do not fight them
Accept them and find a way to help and teach them through love
why: Marcus Aurelius's counsel: love itself teaches the road to virtue.

title: Word-opening
steps: Take one Greek word
Unpack its letters, sounds and parts
Draw out the teaching encoded in it
why: Following Proclus, the signified can be reached through the signifier.

title: Read in the original
steps: Read Greek (or Sanskrit) texts in the original where possible
Attend to sound and syntax, not only concepts
why: The language works on brain, soul and energy like music or mantra.

title: Ethics as energy hygiene
steps: Notice thoughts, desires and emotions that block your flow
Treat these as the real non-virtue
Restore free flow
why: Virtue is the easy flow of the soul.

title: Look for the dharma in your own root
steps: Before running East, study your own tradition
Look for the practices hidden in its texts
why: Everything you seek is where you started.

title: Find the weed
steps: Take any pathology: violence, war, ecological damage
Look for its root
Name the separateness between me and the other
why: One cause, one cure: knowing ourselves as love.

title: Read crisis as a cut
steps: See a crisis as a cut between past and future
Watch for new ideas hatching in it
Turn back to the inner source of fullness
why: Crisis is the cradle of renaissance.

title: Find your own Odyssey
steps: Ask where you are in your journey
Name your Ithaca, your inner centre
Seek Athena's guidance: philosophy and self-knowledge
why: The classics are symbols of the soul's journey.

title: The vocation test
steps: Ask what makes you feel whole
Ask what makes you lose sense of time
Follow that, leaving money aside
why: Those two signs show where love is, what the soul loves.

title: Three-stage Hellenic meditation
steps: Stochasmos: put one object, idea, goal or quality at the centre of consciousness and study it without the senses
Dialogismos: let awareness expand through that field and wait for a conception or aha moment
Theoria: let subject, object and process merge
why: A developmental Hellenic path from focus to non-dual gnosis.

title: Character work
steps: Locate the seats of your emotions in the body
Cultivate inner strength and resilience
Train the mind toward the harmonious and the heart toward positive emotion
Tame desires so they serve the soul
why: Ethics as moulding character, whether rebuilding when old or building when young.

title: Move happiness inward
steps: Notice where you have invested happiness in objects, situations or the body
Move that foundation to your self
why: Everything material can be taken away; the self cannot.

title: Prepare for the transition in peacetime
steps: Cultivate courage and clarity now
Practise the ability to separate from the body
Treat it like clearing snow you know will fall
why: We will be held to account if we knew and did not prepare; death is a transition that needs a warrior.

title: Clean the soul's monsters now
steps: Use meditation, hymns and spiritual work
Face each cowardice, anger and rage while alive
why: After death the soul meets its own etheric imprints as monsters; cleaned now, the passage is not frightening.

title: Purity before power
steps: Lay a base of purity (ἀγνότης) and blameless virtue
Only then raise your vital force
Put that force at the service of wisdom, the polity and your soul, never of passing passions
why: Without purity Ares becomes the black horse; with it the red fire rises into the golden helmet.

title: Red boundaries
steps: Keep wisdom at your centre
Set clear boundaries at your edges
Guard your gains and virtues
Call people who protect you your ἕρκος
why: Creation, the soul and awakening all need guarding: the greater the treasure, the higher the walls.

title: Meet attacks with inner Arean energy
steps: Do not shout or hit
Let your aura carry Ares' force
Speak to the tyrant in the only language it understands
why: Even your embrace and your peace should 'have roots'.

title: The daily Ares audit
steps: Ask: where did my vital energy go in these 24 hours?
Ask: whom does my warrior serve, which fortress, polity or mentality?
why: Ares is our working force; we must know what we give it to.

title: Stand up and act
steps: After meditation, add Ares: stand up
Turn insight into work and action
why: Meditation alone works mind and feeling; awakening that does not become life is incomplete.

title: Read the hymn to Ares
steps: Read or chant the Orphic hymn to Ares
Use it for clarity when emotional currents fog you
She recommends it for immune problems
why: In her view the hymn wakes decisiveness, fearlessness, boundaries, θάρσος and health; the health use is her recommendation, not a medical claim.

title: Work with the rainbow
steps: Contemplate the rainbow as a symbol
Place wisdom at the centre and red at the edges
why: The rainbow maps the seven strata of the world, with Ares as the outer band.

title: Know-the-knower meditation
steps: Turn consciousness back on itself
Ask: Where am I? What am I? What am I made of? Who thinks? Who is ὁ νοῶν?
Think the νόησις you are; become aware of the awareness you are
Notice you find no person or thing, only boundlessness, freedom, timelessness and peace
Repeat it
why: She calls it easy and doable now; repeated, it may open the exit of the cave.

title: Dis-identify
steps: Tell yourself: I have thoughts, emotions, desires and a body
Recall how your body has changed while the 'I' stayed
Rest as the one who is aware of them
why: You are not what you have.

title: Stop looking for the exit outside
steps: Notice when you search the senses or circumstances for a way out
Turn all your attention inward instead
why: Banging on the cave wall only takes you deeper; you are the gate.

title: Watch the shadow theatre
steps: Look behind the veil of events and news
Watch joys, sorrows and festivals as a shadow play
Remember: I am not this; I am this too, but more
why: Not identifying with what happens outside is the turn itself.

title: The ἔστω exercise
steps: As a working hypothesis, say: let everything be perfect and just
Assume this must happen for some reason
Remember you are partway up the mountain and cannot see all the folds
Allow that it may bring many good things
Say 'let it be' and let go
why: Acceptance opens the personality to the true self, because the ego is resistance.

title: Read your exhaustion as a signal
steps: Notice being fed up and the thought 'this can't be all'
Treat it as the push to start searching for what is true
why: Pain is the perfect motive to lead us to truth.

title: Self-inquiry by the criterion of truth
steps: Test your body, emotions, desires and thoughts: does each stay unchanged?
Ask: what in me does not change?
Answer from experience, not from what someone said
why: Only what does not change meets the criterion of truth.

title: Turn inward and find 'I am'
steps: Close eyes, ears and mouth to the outside
Attend to what stays stable while everything changes
Notice the same 'I am' at 5, 20 and 100
Remain there: this is the apprenticeship that gestates the new birth
why: Staying in the inward turn carries the second birth to term.

title: Prepare the soil of the soul
steps: Cultivate virtues that make the soul gentle and fertile
Let it receive the seed of the spirit
why: The soul is cultivated like land.

title: Do not force awakening
steps: Keep practising without scheduling the result
Expect it 'suddenly'
why: Its hour cannot be programmed: it is Plato's ἐξαίφνης.

title: Die before you die, then return
steps: Practise the death of the illusory self
After awakening, go back into ordinary life
Recognise the One in every form
why: The journey ends with a return, not a fairy tale.

title: Speak with light
steps: Before speaking of anything sacred, light the fire of the inner hearth at the centre of the heart
Let that light spread through your body
Let it become your words
why: The first Pythagorean symbol: do not speak of Pythagorean things without light.

title: Bear fate and heal
steps: Meet what fate brings without indignation
Heal what you can
Keep a sacred distance, stillness and observation
why: From the Golden Verses: the virtues let us meet events without attaching our identity to them.

title: Start with the heart
steps: Purify the heart of passions
Practise cosmic love in daily life
why: Philosophy as φιλότης starts in the heart.

title: After every insight, work
steps: Ask which channel suits your soul (art, science, care, law, solidarity)
Express the insight there
why: Awakening must be embodied, personally and politically.

title: Learn to listen
steps: Listen to the Golden Verses as vibration, not only information
why: Pythagoras' school was a hall of listening together.

title: Notice the observer
steps: Notice that something in you always watches what you live
Recognise it as logos, the energy of consciousness
why: Logos is not thinking but the one who observes.

title: The name as mantra
steps: Write ΠΥΘΑΓΟΡΑΣ in archaic capitals in your notebook
Count its nine letters
Treat the name as an ideogram or mantra
why: The name, read through the temple's three levels, says: you are Pythagoras.

title: Decide to know yourself
steps: Say: 'I want to know myself'
Move your focus from outside to inside
Give your inner world the attention you would give a loved one's heart
why: The desire to know is the first step of knowledge; attention opens the inner world.

title: Daily self-observation
steps: Ask: what am I desiring, what am I feeling?
What emotion did I just express, and what quality did it have?
Catch daydreaming: where did this thought start and where is it going?
Notice your habitual disposition: optimistic, gloomy, angry, melancholic, cheerful
why: This 'extremely therapeutic' stage restores the soul's free flow.

title: Replant your habits
steps: With clear intention, stop expressing traits that do not help you
In place of an old bad habit, sow and plant a good one
why: Move from passive observer to active maker of your character.

title: Loosen your labels
steps: List the roles you identify with: name, profession, parent, nationality
Notice how attached you are to each
why: Shedding roles hurts in proportion to identification; labels cramp the divine self.

title: Use confinement as ascesis
steps: Ask where the basis of your being well really is
Re-examine what is worth something
why: When externals close overnight, the basis turns out to be within.

title: Govern yourself first
steps: Practise self-mastery before trying to govern anything outside you
why: The soul is the first polity.

title: Gratitude and thanksgiving
steps: Close each day or lesson with gratitude
Pair your effort with openness to grace: 'with Athena, move your hand too'
why: Thanksgiving activates grace, the incalculable factor in eudaimonia.

title: Celebrate freedom in the present
steps: Turn attention from past dates to the now
Treat freedom as the present state of your existence
why: Freedom as memory is not freedom lived.

title: Say «No» within
steps: Name an old state or passion that tosses you about
Say «No» to it, removing rather than acquiring
why: Every subtraction is a «No», and truth is reached by subtraction.

title: Plant a «Yes» after every «No»
steps: After refusing something, ask what you will build instead
Tend the soil: water, prune, be patient
why: A «No» without a «Yes» is lame and stays locked to what it opposes.

title: Watch your yeses and noes
steps: Notice each yes and no in your day
See that their sum sets your course
why: Like Heracles at the crossroads, we choose at every moment.

title: Refuse ἰδιώτευσις
steps: Do not shrink into your small circle
Feel responsible for the whole earth, as Kazantzakis did
why: The idiot forgets he is one with all.

title: Make yourself lovable
steps: Walk among the antiquities
Read the ancients
Listen to harmonious music
Wake up and look at the sun
Do not take Greece or the Aegean for granted
why: Be the change you want to see; eros is activated by the καλόν.

title: Speak simply
steps: Prefer simple words to academic complexity
why: Simplicity is the easiest road to truth.

title: Bring a concept to mind
steps: Bring a concept to mind: love, Apollo, light
Notice what changed around you and inside you
Ask whether you can touch or hear it
Recognise that you 'see' it noetically, not with the eyes
why: Awakening, like any idea, is noetic: it cannot be pointed at, only seen inwardly.

title: Admit that you do not know
steps: Recognise honestly that you do not know
Let that make you ask, as the restless prisoner asks whether things are as he was told
why: Asking opens the pores (ἀπορία), and Apollo begins to reveal himself.

title: Want to change
steps: Notice where you are stuck
Form the intention and will to change
Let the stagnant waters flow
why: Healing starts with ρ, flow: nothing moves until you will it.

title: Wash away views and habits
steps: Notice the habits, stances and ways of seeing that create suffering and war in your life
Remove them, as Apollo washes away and destroys only the useless
why: As the veils are cleaned, clarity and luminosity appear.

title: Meditate into emptiness
steps: Do not fill meditation with images, like imagining the kitchen and cooking
Go toward purity of mind by removing content
why: Pure nous resting in itself is meditation without content.

title: Listen in silence for the answer
steps: Ask, then stop analysing
Let an answer or awareness appear
Trust what the heart says first, then the mind
why: This is mantic, unmediated knowing: each of us is a seer.

title: Choose one direction
steps: Decide between vice and virtue
Drop πολυπραγμοσύνη, wanting to do everything
Keep one target, like the diamond made of one element
why: At the archer's step the will stops changing.

title: Stabilise the flashes
steps: Welcome signs and 'wow' moments without chasing them
Build a philosophical, virtuous and musical way of life around them
Hold it with a steady will
why: 'It is raining awakenings'; what matters is a stable way of life.

title: Do not fear opposition
steps: Stop avoiding conflict
Look for the union of the opposites you face
why: Harmony is made from opposites, not by removing them.

title: Live for the common good
steps: On waking, ask what you will do for the whole, not only your own circle
Notice what you do only to maintain an imaginary persona
Gather with others in dialogue and philosophy
why: The last step is 'not I but we'.

title: Know eros instead of avoiding it
steps: Get to know eros truly and from within
Live and apply it
Do so under a wisdom teaching that gives tools and criteria
why: Then eros lifts you instead of burning you.

title: Treat yourself with sacredness
steps: Show sacredness toward yourself
Notice how it changes your respect for your partners, and the reverse
why: As we treat our partners within, so we treat our partners without.

title: Meet every being with reverence and remembrance
steps: Approach every being with reverence (σεπτότης)
Look with an awakened gaze that remembers Being is common and already εὐδαίμων
why: It changes how your inner psychic energy moves.

title: Steer eros with the divine nous
steps: Apply eros with awareness
Use the divine nous, not the calculating mind
Turn the rudder of the erotic impulse toward its natural goal
why: So eros leads where nature set it to lead.

title: Leave nothing out of the path
steps: Do not make eros the one exception to freedom
Illuminate and harmonise all the forces of the soul, erotic ones included
why: A holistic path excludes nothing of ontological importance.

title: Diagnose a society by its eros
steps: Ask from which energy centre its citizens approach eros
Ask with what vision and from what consciousness
Compare which kinds of eros different regimes promote
why: As we approach eros, so we approach our life together.
